pageCache.text:
Welcome
to Chilworth
Nestled between St Martha’s on the Hill and Blackheath is our Infant School and Nursery welcoming children ages 2-7.
A new sensory space at our nursery!
Our Woodland Cabin opened in May 2025.
Video Tour: Experience the beautiful surroundings and facilities of Chilworth C of E Infant School & Nursery with our Headteacher, Coralie.
Welcome to Chilworth Church of England Infant School in Guildford, Surrey. We are a one form entry village school with a popular attached nursery providing quality education for children from 2-7 yrs.
At Chilworth, our vision is to create a safe, caring Christian environment where every child develops a love of life and learning. Our school values of love, life and welcome are at the heart of everything we do, brought to life with enthusiasm, professionalism and dedication by our wonderful team.
A warm welcome from our Headteacher, Coralie
I am very proud and privileged to be the Headteacher of this wonderful Infant and Nursery school.
At Chilworth we want our children to not only love learning but to show love to those around them. Our young children are the life of our community and we want to offer them a school experience that gives them life in all its fullness. Chilworth School is a welcoming environment where everyone is valued and we extend this welcome to you!
We have a friendly, caring and dedicated staff who provide an excellent education for the children in their care. We offer an exciting, hands-on curriculum which is designed to meet every child’s needs.
Chilworth C of E Infant School is a wonderful environment for children to start their school journey. Although our school premises may look small, we are fortunate that our buildings are set in extensive grounds, fully enclosed for safety and security. Each classroom has covered areas to enable outdoor learning whatever the weather. Our grounds include a sizeable sports field, a pond, a large playground with trim trail and a swimming pool!
Parents are highly supportive of the school. As well as volunteering as reading helpers and accompanying us on trips, they run a fabulous PTA raising vital funds for the school. A website can only give you a flavour of all we have to offer – tours are always welcome so please call the office to organise a time to visit – you will be most welcome!
Mrs Coralie MankelHeadteacher
Love, Life, Welcome.
Drawing synergies from nature, education, and community, Chilworth Church of England Infant School & Nursery stands as a beacon of excellence in early childhood education, expanding young horizons and striving to create lifelong learners who cherish their environment through shared Christian values.
My best memory of school is playing with my friends and my teacher.
My best memory of school is when we made tiffin and when we do science.
My best memory of school is going on the equipment in the hall, and Craft Day!
I love Chilworth because we get to do lots of fun stuff like swimming and outside learning
My favourite memory was recreating The Great Fire of London with a real fire!
Making mud pies and Funsplash are the best things!
Extra fun for everyone!
Involve your children in a variety of engaging clubs at Chilworth Infant School. We have ActivSport after school promoting active fun, a convenient Breakfast Club for early drop-offs, BoogiePumps dance classes, Planet Soccer, Holly King performing arts and Recorder Club for creative exploration.
Visit the school
Your child's happiness and education is key. A guided tour is the best way to discover what we can provide for them.

Subjects > Music
Curriculum focus
Music
Music inspires one of the highest forms of creativity and is life enhancing whether there is a love of classical, pop or jazz. Pupils should be introduced to a wide range of recorded music whilst exploring their own musical expression through singing, playing instruments or through dance. Music is medicine for the mind.
Intent
Our music curriculum at Chilworth C of E Infant School is dedicated to nurturing the musicians of the 21st century. Our approach to music education is broad, modern and ambitious encompassing music appreciation, musical theory alongside playing tuned and untuned instruments all underpinned with singing a wide range of songs.
Our primary goal is to allow children to experience and engage in music making in all its diversity. We understand the importance of appreciating music alongside participating in musical activities.
At Chilworth, we are fortunate to have a specialist music teacher but we also enable all teachers to feel confident teaching music to their pupils.
Implementation
Our scheme of work covers the three areas of the National Curriculum: performing playing, performing singing and improvising & experimenting. These are taught in discrete weekly lessons enabling the children to understand and apply fundamental principles of the three areas. Using the children friendly “Charanga” online programme from Surrey Arts Music, our infant children are able to sing, move and make music. They are also given the opportunity to listen to recorded and live music. This includes trips to concerts as well as visiting musicians.
Outside of discrete music sessions children have plenty of musical opportunities whether that is singing as part our Collective Worship to music making in the EYFS as part of their continuous provision. KS1 pupils perform in regular Christmas and end of year musical extravaganzas as well as during their special services at the local church.
Children can also further their skills by joining our extra-curricular recorder club and choir

Subjects > Science
Curriculum focus
Science
“The scientist is not a person who gives right answers, they’re the ones who asks the right questions.”
Intent
At Chilworth Infant C of E School, our intent is to foster a deep curiosity for Science among our pupils, particularly focusing on exploring the natural world in our local environment. We aim for children to develop a solid understanding of scientific processes across Physics, Biology, and Chemistry. By gaining a strong foundation in scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding, our students will be equipped to appreciate the relevance of science both now and in the future.
Implementation
Our curriculum is carefully structured to build knowledge incrementally from Nursery to Year 2, with key areas of learning identified and reinforced over time. Through our "Think back Thursday" sessions, we ensure that learning is consolidated and embedded. Hands-on exploration is central to our approach, with children engaging in practical activities to deepen their understanding of scientific concepts. Good enquiry practice encourages children to ask questions, fostering curiosity and promoting deeper learning.
Our school is ideally located near the Surrey Hills, providing rich opportunities for firsthand experiences within nature. All year groups have access to this resource, which enhances their learning in Science. Well-resourced science areas enable children to not only observe scientific phenomena but also conduct experiments to answer their own questions. We utilize ICT equipment and software to record data and share findings using scientific language, enhancing both scientific literacy and digital skills.
Additionally, class growing areas allow children to develop a closer connection to nature, fostering a sense of responsibility for the flora and fauna within our school grounds.
Impact
As a result of our Science Curriculum, children are empowered to explore the world around them and formulate their own questions using appropriate scientific language. They approach investigations purposefully, driven by a desire to uncover scientific truths through experimentation and analysis. With age-appropriate scientific knowledge, pupils are able to apply their understanding across the curriculum, enriching subjects such as Design and Technology, Forest School, and PSHE. Our aim is for children to leave our school with a deep-seated curiosity for the world and a strong foundation in scientific thinking that will serve them well in their future endeavours.
Early Learning Goal for the end of Reception
• Explore the natural world around them making observations and drawing pictures of animals and plants
• Know some of the similarities and differences between the natural world around them and contrasting environments, drawing on their experiences and what has been read in class
• Understand some important processes and changes in the natural world around them, including the seasons and changing states of matter
National curriculum goals - Year 1 and 2
During years 1 and 2, pupils should be taught to use the following practical scientific methods, processes and skills through the teaching of the programme of study content:
• Asking simple questions and recognising that they can be answered in different ways
• Observing closely, using simple equipment
• Performing simple tests
• Identifying and classifying
• Using their observations and ideas to suggest answers to questions
• Gathering and recording data to help in answering question

Subjects> Art and Design
Curriculum focus
Art and Design
Art inspires one of the highest forms of creativity and is life enhancing. Pupils should be introduced to a wide range of Artists and techniques whilst exploring their own artist expression through exploring different mediums.
Intent
At Chilworth Infant C of E School, our intent is to foster a deep enjoyment for Art among our pupils, particularly focusing on developing creativity alongside fine motor skills to enable competence in all areas of the art curriculum. We introduce children to a wide range of Artists and techniques whilst developing their own artist expression through exploring different mediums. By gaining a strong foundation in different artistic techniques, our students will be equipped to appreciate artists’ work whilst also expressing themselves through art.
Implementation
Our curriculum is carefully structured to build knowledge incrementally from Nursery to Year 2, with key areas of learning identified and reinforced over time. Through our "Think back Thursday" sessions, we ensure that learning is consolidated and embedded. Hands-on exploration is central to our approach, with children engaging in practical activities as well as art appreciation.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage Children at the expected level of development will:
Safely use and explore a variety of materials, tools and techniques, experimenting with colour, design, texture, form, and function
Share their creations, explaining the process they have used
Make use of props and materials when role playing characters in narratives and stories
In Key Stage One our well planning learning journeys for art and design ensure that all pupils:
produce creative work, exploring their ideas and recording their experiences
become proficient in drawing, painting, sculpture and other art, craft and design techniques
evaluate and analyse creative works using the language of art, craft and design
know about great artists, craft makers and designers, and understand the historical and cultural development of their art forms.
We utilize ICT equipment and software to support our art curriculum. This may be to research artists as well as creating digitally produced artwork.
Impact
As a result of our Art Curriculum, children are empowered to appreciate the way others interpret the world around them through art and formulate their own appreciation using appropriate artistic language. They approach art projects sequentially learning skills and techniques culminating in a final piece. With age-appropriate artistic knowledge, pupils are able to apply their skills across the curriculum, enriching subjects such as Design and Technology. Our aim is for children to leave our school with a deep appreciation for creative expression as well as an ability to apply artistic processes so this can serve them well in their future endeavours.
Early learning goals for the end of EYFS
Children at the expected level of development will:
Safely use and explore a variety of materials, tools and techniques, experimenting with colour, design, texture, form, and function
Share their creations, explaining the process they have used
Make use of props and materials when role playing characters in narratives and stories
The national curriculum for art and design aims to ensure that all pupils:
produce creative work, exploring their ideas and recording their experiences
become proficient in drawing, painting, sculpture and other art, craft and design techniques
evaluate and analyse creative works using the language of art, craft and design
know about great artists, craft makers and designers, and understand the historical and cultural development of their art forms.

Subjects> Computing
Curriculum focus
Computing
The computing curriculum allows children to learn how to participate in a fully digital world.
Intent
Our computing curriculum at Chilworth C of E Infant School is dedicated to nurturing the thinkers of the 21st century. Our approach to computing education is modern, ambitious, and tailored to the needs of today's digital landscape.
Our primary goal is to empower students with computational thinking and foster creativity, equipping them to actively engage in the digital world. We understand the importance of keeping pace with ever-evolving technology while ensuring that our students grasp both its benefits and challenges.
At Chilworth, we prioritise cultivating respectful, responsible, and confident technology users. We emphasize the significance of online safety measures, ensuring that children develop a keen awareness of how to safeguard themselves and others in the digital realm.
Implementation
Our scheme of work covers the three areas of the National Curriculum: Computer Science, Information Technology and Digital Literacy. These are taught in discrete weekly lessons enabling the children to understand and apply fundamental principles of the three strands. Using the children friendly “Espresso Coding” online programme from Discovery Education, our infant children are able to create but also debug simple programmes. They are also given the opportunity to predict different programmes’ behaviours.
Outside of discrete computing sessions children produce their own digital exercise books using “Book Creator”. The use of Book Creator enables the children to use technology across the whole curriculum purposefully to create, organise, store and retrieve their learning.
At Chilworth C of E Infant School, when it comes to Digital Literacy our children are taught the “SMART” rules
· S encourages young people to be safe by not giving out their personal details online
· M draws attention to the risks associated with meeting someone you only know online
· A highlights the risks of accepting emails, pictures and text messages from unknown sources
· R is a reminder that not all information found online is necessarily reliable
· T encourages children to tell someone if something happens or they meet someone online that makes them feel uncomfortable
Children put these skills into practice with the use of Microsoft Team where they are able to safely interact with each other and staff in a closed online environment preparing them for a online digital life.
Impact
Thank to our well-designed computing curriculum, children are ready to engage appropriately, safely and respectfully with technology suitable for their age but with an understanding of how their use of technology will change as they get older.
Children are able to choose the correct hardware and software to show and indeed learn new concepts. Children are able to make suitable programmes that achieve a fully understood purpose.
Children engage in learning activities which they would have found more challenging, if not impossible, without the use of technology.
The national curriculum for computing aims to ensure that all pupils:
Can understand and apply the fundamental principles and concepts of computer science, including abstraction, logic, algorithms and data representation
Can analyse problems in computational terms, and have repeated practical experience of writing computer programs in order to solve such problems
Can evaluate and apply information technology, including new or unfamiliar technologies, analytically to solve problems
Are responsible, competent, confident and creative users of information and communication technology

Subjects> Geography
Curriculum focus
Geography
Geography explains the past, illuminates the present and prepares us for the future. The study of Geography is one which should inspire pupils with a curiosity and respect for the diverse range of people, countries and traditions that make up the world. Additionally, it is hoped that the study of Geography will provide the children with an understanding of the environmental issues of the world and ways in which we can preserve the world for generations to come.
Intent
At Chilworth C of E Infant School we begin teaching geography in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) by helping children understand the world around them, primarily through getting out into the great outdoors. Firsthand experience helps children understand ‘place’, starting with the familiarity of their home and school to the village of Chilworth and beyond.
In Key Stage One children learn about where Chilworth is positioned within the United Kingdom. They explore features of their village locality as well as the Chilworth Gunpowder Mills behind our school. With a sense of location firmly established, pupils can learn about other countries and continents exploring similarities and differences to their personal experience of living in a leafy Surrey village.
Implementation
We have designed our own geography curriculum based on Development Matters and the National Curriculum. We begin teaching geography from the starting point of each child’s sense of place and belonging in their immediate environment. We seek to widen their knowledge and horizons through geographical enquiry. We use the geography of Chilworth as a starting point of learning wherever possible. We go on local walks to explore the features of our surroundings and learn the geographical vocabulary to help pupils make sense of their world. We ensure that each geography learning journey builds on the skills and knowledge already taught in previous year groups as well as ensuring that our pupils are prepared for the geographical enquiry they will encounter in Key Stage Two. Through well designed retrieval activities we assess each child’s knowledge and understanding of their geography units.
Impact
Our carefully planned learning journeys and lessons include hands-on learning as well as a range of different resources alongside opportunities to reflect on learning. As a result, pupils are able to retain much of their geographical learning. The geographical knowledge that pupils at Chilworth acquire is both personal and meaningful, ensuring a strong likelihood that much of it will remain part of their foundational knowledge of the world as they continue on their educational journey.
Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
Early Learning Goals (ELG)
Understanding the world
Children at the expected level of development will:
People Culture and Communities
Describe their immediate environment using knowledge from observation, discussion, stories, non-fiction texts, and maps; Explain some similarities and differences between life in this country and life in other countries, drawing on knowledge from stories, non-fiction texts and when appropriate maps.
The natural world
Know some similarities and differences between the natural world around them and contrasting environments, drawing on their experiences and what has been read in class; Understand some important processes and changes in the natural world around them, including the seasons and changing states of matter.

Subjects > History
Curriculum focus
History
The more you know about the past, the better prepared you are for the future.
Intent
At Chilworth C of E Infant School we begin teaching history in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) by helping children understand the past, primarily through storytelling. Stories allow children to understand that events are in the past. Adults can help children to explore key figures or events and begin to understand their importance.
In Key Stage One children learn about changes within living memory as well as events beyond living memory that are significant nationally or globally. They build on the knowledge and understanding of their own place in the world, progressing to a recognition of the place of others in history.
Implementation
We have designed our own history curriculum based on Development Matters and the National Curriculum. We begin teaching history from the starting point of each child’s sense of place and belonging in their immediate environment. We seek to widen their knowledge and horizons through historical enquiry. We use the history of Chilworth as a starting point of historical enquiry wherever possible. We invite visitors from the local historical society to share artefacts and knowledge with the children and we take classes out on local walks to gain firsthand experience. Wherever possible we take advantage of loan boxes from local museums. We ensure that each history learning journey builds on the skills and knowledge already taught in previous year groups as well as ensuring that our pupils are prepared for the historical enquiry they will encounter in Key Stage Two. Through well designed retrieval activities we assess each child’s knowledge and understanding of their history units.
Impact
Our carefully planned learning journeys and lessons include hands-on learning as well as a range of different resources alongside opportunities to reflect on learning. As a result, pupils are able to retain much of their historical learning. The historical knowledge that pupils at Chilworth acquire is both personal and meaningful ensuring a strong likelihood that much of it will remain part of their foundational knowledge of the world as they continue on their educational journey.
Early learning goals (ELG)
Talk about the lives of the people around them and their roles in society
Know some similarities and differences between things in the past and now, drawing on their experiences and what has been read in class
Understand the past through settings, characters and events encountered in books read in class and storytelling
National curriculum
Pupils should be taught about:
changes within living memory. Where appropriate, these should be used to reveal aspects of change in national life
events beyond living memory that are significant nationally or globally (for example, the Great Fire of London, the first aeroplane flight or events commemorated through festivals or anniversaries)

Subjects > Mathematics
Curriculum focus
Mathematics
"In mathematics the art of proposing a question must be held of higher value than solving it"
Intent
The aim of our maths curriculum is for children from Nursery to Year 2 to become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics. They will be able to apply the necessary skills to reason and solve a variety of problems. The focus is to develop a love of maths and positive attitudes to the subject by recognising that mistakes are part of the learning process.
We implement our maths curriculum through the use of a variety of teaching and learning styles. We follow a mastery approach that is closely linked to the White Rose Hub planning. The curriculum is divided into blocks of learning focused around different areas of maths and allows children to spend sufficient time on a concept to fully understand it and apply their knowledge. The blocks of learning, and individual lessons ensure children have the prior knowledge required for new learning. Lessons include elements of fluency, reasoning and problem solving so children have a deep understanding of concepts within the lesson. During our lessons, models and images are used to support learning in each area and enable the children to progress from concrete to pictorial to abstract. Assessment is used regularly to ensure that children are secure in their mathematical learning and to identify any gaps before moving forward.
Impact
Our children make good progress as they journey from Nursery to Year 2. Children leave our school with a positive attitude to maths and a willingness to have a go. Our children have the fundamental skills to prepare them for the next stage of their mathematics education.

Subjects> Reading
Curriculum focus
Reading
At Chilworth C of E Infant School, we believe that every child has the right to learn to read and become a confident, competent reader. We believe reading is the key that unlocks the rest of the curriculum. We believe children must have access to high quality texts that develop a child’s imagination, deepens their receptive and expressive vocabulary and helps children to understand the world they live in. We believe that reading for pleasure is vital and it is our aim for all children to develop a life-long love of reading.
Intent
Phonics (reading and spelling)
At Chilworth C of E Infant School, we believe that all our children can become fluent readers and writers. This is why we teach reading through Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which is a systematic and synthetic phonics programme. We start teaching phonics in Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised programme, which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.
As a result, all our children are able to tackle any unfamiliar words as they read. At Chilworth C of E Infant School, we also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside of the phonics lesson and across the curriculum. We have a strong focus on language development for our children because we know that speaking and listening are crucial skills for reading and writing in all subjects.
Comprehension
At Chilworth C of E Infant School we value reading as a crucial life skill. By the time children leave us, they read confidently for meaning and regularly enjoy reading for pleasure. Our readers are equipped with the tools to tackle unfamiliar vocabulary. We encourage our children to see themselves as readers for both pleasure and purpose.
Because we believe teaching every child to read is so important, we have a Reading Leader who drives the early reading programme in our school. This person is highly skilled at teaching phonics and reading, and they monitor and support our reading team, so everyone teaches with fidelity to the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised Programme.
Implementation
Foundations for phonics in Nursery
We provide a balance of child-led and adult-led experiences for all children that meet the curriculum expectations for ‘Communication and language’ and ‘Literacy’. These include:
Sharing high-quality stories and poems
Learning a range of nursery rhymes and action rhymes
Activities that develop focused listening and attention, including oral blending
Attention to high-quality language
We ensure Nursery children are well prepared to begin learning grapheme-phoneme correspondences (GPCs) and blending in Reception
Daily phonics lessons in Reception and Year 1
We teach phonics for 30 minutes a day. In Reception, we build from 10-minute lessons, with additional daily oral blending games, to the full-length lesson as quickly as possible. Each Friday, we review the week’s teaching to help children become fluent readers.
Children make a strong start in Reception: teaching begins in Week 2 of the Autumn term.
We follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised Programme:
Children in Reception are taught to read and spell words using Phase 2 and 3 GPCs, and words with adjacent consonants (Phase 4) with fluency and accuracy
Children in Year 1 review Phases 3 and 4 and are taught to read and spell words using Phase 5 GPCs with fluency and accuracy
Daily Keep-up lessons ensure every child learns to read
Any child who needs additional practice has daily Keep-up support, taught by a fully trained adult. Keep-up lessons match the structure of class teaching, and use the same procedures, resources and mantras, but in smaller steps with more repetition, so that every child secures their learning.
We timetable daily phonics lessons for any child in Year 2 who is not fully fluent at reading or has not passed the Phonics screening check. These children urgently need to catch up, so the gap between themselves and their peers does not widen. We use the Rapid Catch-up assessments to identify the gaps in their phonic knowledge and teach to these using the Rapid Catch-up resources – at pace.
These short, sharp lessons last 15-20 minutes daily and have been designed to ensure children quickly catch up to age-related expectations in reading.
Teaching reading: Reading practice sessions three times a week
We teach children to read through reading practice sessions three times a week.
Are taught by a fully trained adult to small groups of approximately six children
Use books matched to the children’s secure phonic knowledge using the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised assessments and book matching grids on pages 11–20 of ‘Application of phonics to reading’
Are monitored by the class teacher, who rotates and works with each group on a regular basis
Each reading practice session has a clear focus, so that the demands of the session do not overload the children’s working memory. The reading practice sessions have been designed to focus on three key reading skills:
Prosody: teaching children to read with understanding and expression
Comprehension: teaching children to understand the text.
In Reception these sessions start in Week 4. Children who are not yet decoding have daily additional blending practice in small groups, so that they quickly learn to blend and can begin to read books.
In Year 2 we continue to teach reading in this way for any children who still need to practice reading with decodable books.
Home reading
The decodable reading practice book is taken home to ensure success is shared with the family.
Reading for pleasure books also go home for parents to share and read to children. We share the research behind the importance and impact of sharing quality children’s books with parents through workshops, leaflets and the Everybody read!
We use the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised parents’ resources to engage our families and share information about phonics, the benefits of sharing books, how children learn to blend and other aspects of our provision, both online and through workshops.
Additional reading support for vulnerable children
Children in Reception and Year 1 who are receiving additional phonics Keep-up sessions read their reading practice book to an adult daily.
Ensuring consistency and pace of progress
Every teacher in our school has been trained to teach reading, so we have the same expectations of progress. We all use the same language, routines and resources to teach children to read so that we lower children’s cognitive load.
Weekly content grids map each element of new learning to each day, week and term for the duration of the programme.
Lesson templates, Prompt cards and ‘How to’ videos ensure teachers all have a consistent approach and structure for each lesson.
The Reading Leader and SLT use the Audit and Prompt cards to regularly monitor and observe teaching; they use the summative data to identify children who need additional support and gaps in learning.
Ensuring reading for pleasure
‘Reading for pleasure is the single most important indicator of a child’s success.’ (OECD 2002)
‘The will influences the skill and vice versa.’ (OECD 2010)
To promote and ensure reading for pleasure:
We value reading for pleasure highly
Teaching staff read high quality texts to the children every day
Every classroom has an inviting reading corner that encourages a love for reading
We ensure our reading corners are stocked with high quality books that engage all readers. There is an abundance of traditional tales, children's classics, modern texts, non-fiction books and poetry. We are constantly reviewing and refreshing our stock to ensure the books on offer encourage children to discover the world around them and embrace the diversity, variety of cultures and experiences the world has to offer
Children explore books that are written by renowned authors, are rich in language and present the challenges and delights of the world they are growing up in
We believe it is our responsibility to support children in developing an understanding of theirself, their emotions and ways to effectively communicate their thoughts and feelings. We offer children the opportunity to explore books that encourage each child to be themselves and be proud of who they are
We use the Everybody read! resources to grow our teachers’ knowledge of current books, the most recent research and to grow our own Reading for Pleasure practice
Impact
Assessment
Assessment is used to monitor progress and to identify any child needing additional support as soon as they need it.
Assessment for learning is used:
Daily within class to identify children needing Keep-up support
Weekly in the Review lesson to assess gaps, address these immediately and secure fluency of GPCs, words and spellings
Summative assessment for Reception and Year 1 is used:
Every six weeks to assess progress, to identify gaps in learning that need to be addressed, to identify any children needing additional support and to plan the Keep-up support that they need
By SLT and scrutinised through the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised assessment tracker, to narrow attainment gaps between different groups of children and so that any additional support for teachers can be put into place
Fluency assessments measure children’s accuracy and reading speed in short one-minute assessments.
In Year 1, when children are reading the Phase 5 set 3, 4 and 5 books
With children following the Rapid Catch-up programme in Years 2, when they are reading the Phase 5 set 3, 4 and 5 books
To assess when children are ready to exit the programme. For Year 1 children, this is when they read the final fluency assessment at 60–70+ words per minute. Older children can exit the Rapid Catch-up programme when they read the final fluency assessment at 90+ words per minute. At these levels, children should have sufficient fluency to tackle any book at age-related expectations. After exiting the programme, children do not need to read any more fully decodable books
A placement assessment is used:
With any child new to the school to quickly identify any gaps in their phonic knowledge and plan and provide appropriate extra teaching
The Rapid Catch-up assessment is used:
With any child new to the school in Year 2 to quickly identify any gaps in their phonic knowledge and plan and provide appropriate extra teaching.
Statutory assessment
Children in Year 1 sit the Phonics screening check. Any child not passing the check re-sits it in Year 2.
Ongoing assessment for Rapid Catch-up in Year 2
Children in Year 2 are assessed through:
The Rapid Catch-up initial assessment to quickly identify any gaps in their phonic knowledge and plan appropriate teaching
The Rapid Catch-up summative assessments to assess progress and inform teaching
The Rapid Catch-up fluency assessments when children are reading the Phase 5 set 3, 4 and 5 books for age 7+.
The fluency assessments measure children’s accuracy and reading speed in short one-minute assessments. They also assess when children are ready to exit the Rapid Catch-up programme, which is when they read the final fluency assessment at 90+ words per minute

Subjects > Design and Technology
Curriculum focus
Design & Technology
Design and technology aims to develop the creative, technical and practical expertise needed to perform everyday tasks confidently and to participate successfully in an increasingly technological world
Intent
The Design Technology curriculum has been carefully crafted so that all children acquire appropriate subject knowledge, skills and understanding as set out in the National Curriculum. All children have the opportunity through ‘hands on experience’ to be imaginative and to design purposeful products in a varied way. Through DT, children are encouraged to apply and use their developing skills and knowledge to solve a range of problems both as individuals and as part of a team. Design Technology is a way to build resilience to cope when things go wrong and to give children the opportunities, responsibilities, and experiences they need to be successful in later life.
Implementation
Design Technology is a crucial part of school life and learning and it is for this reason that as a school we are dedicated to the teaching and delivery of a high-quality Design Technology curriculum.
This is implemented through:
• A well thought out, whole school, yearly overview of the DT curriculum and skills progression document which allows for progression across year groups in all areas of DT.
• Well planned learning journeys for DT and well-resourced lessons providing children with a hands-on and enriching experience.
• A range of skills being taught incorporating teaching children to be aware of health and safety issues related to the skills they are learning.
• Each unit in KS1 addresses the principles of designing, making, and evaluating and incorporates relevant technical knowledge and understanding in varied contexts.
Early Years Foundation Stage
During the EYFS pupils explore and use a variety of media and materials through a combination of child initiated and adult directed activities. They have the opportunities to learn to:
• Use different media and materials to express their own ideas.
• Use what they have learnt about media and materials in original ways, thinking about form, function and purpose.
• Make plans and construct with a purpose in mind using a variety of resources.
• Develop skills to use simple tools and techniques appropriately, effectively and safely.
• Select appropriate resources for a product and adapt their work where necessary.
• Cook and prepare food adhering to good health and hygiene routines.
Impact
Children will have clear enjoyment and confidence in Design Technology that they will then apply to other areas of the curriculum. Through carefully planned and implemented learning activities the pupils develop the creative, technical and practical expertise needed to perform everyday tasks confidently and to participate successfully in an increasingly technological world. They gain a firm foundation of knowledge and skills to see them equipped to take on further learning in Junior school. Pupil’s skills and knowledge are assessed ongoingly by the class teacher, throughout lessons and a summative assessment is completed after each unit of DT. This informs the Design Technology coordinator of any further areas for curriculum development, pupil support and/or training requirements for staff. EYFS pupils' progress and attainment tells us whether each individual child has met the expected attainment for their age.
Early learning goals (ELG)
Children at the expected level of development will:
Safely use and explore a variety of materials, tools and techniques, experimenting with colour, design, texture, form, and function
Share their creations, explaining the process they have used and make use of props and materials when role playing characters in narratives and stories
The national curriculum for design and technology aims to ensure that all pupils:
Develop the creative, technical and practical expertise needed to perform everyday tasks confidently and to participate successfully in an increasingly technological world
Build and apply a repertoire of knowledge, understanding and skills in order to design and make high quality prototypes and products for a wide range of users
Critique, evaluate and test their ideas and products and the work of others understand and apply the principles of nutrition and learn how to cook

pageCache.pageTitle: Physical Education // Chilworth CofE Infant School

Subjects > Physical Education
Curriculum focus
Physical Education
“Intelligence and skill can only function at the peak of their capacity when the body is healthy and strong.”
Physical education aims to develop competence to excel in a broad range of physical activates, encourage being active for sustained periods of time, and to support children leading healthy, active lives.
Curriculum
Our PE curriculum follows PE Planning which is used by thousands of teachers throughout the UK and overseas to create and deliver high quality primary school PE lessons.
Intent
The national curriculum for physical education aims to ensure that all pupils:
Develop competence to excel in a broad range of physical activities
Are physically active for sustained periods of time
Engage in competitive sports and activities
Lead healthy, active lives.
At Chilworth Infant School and Nursery we believe that Physical Education (PE), experienced in a safe and supportive environment, is essential to ensure children attain optimum physical and emotional development and good health. We intend to deliver high quality teaching and learning opportunities that inspire all children to succeed in physical education and in developing life skills. We want to teach children skills to keep them safe e.g. being able to swim. We also want to teach children how to cooperate and collaborate with others as part of an effective team, understanding fairness and equity of play to embed life-long values. Additionally, an imperative element of the curriculum at Chilworth shows a need for healthy lifestyles, a balanced diet, positive growth mind-set and the resilience to persevere. Our curriculum aims to improve the wellbeing and fitness of all children at Chilworth, not only through the sporting skills taught, but through the underpinning values and disciplines that PE promotes. It is our intention to build a curriculum that enables children to develop knowledge, skills and vocabulary in a broad range of sporting activities, as well as developing values and transferrable life skills such as tolerance, fairness and respect.
Implementation
Our curriculum is planned on a long, medium and short term basis. The long term ensures that the objectives and skills are taught throughout EYFS and key stage 1 and the medium and short term is planned on a half termly and weekly basis.
Impact
We follow ‘PEPlanning’ across the school. Each half term children’s progress and attainment is noted and any adjustments to any future planning are made.

Subjects > Religious Education
Curriculum focus
Religious Education in Church of England Schools
As stated in the Church of England Statement of Entitlement for Religious Education, we aim for all our children to:
Know about and understand Christianity as a diverse global living faith through the exploration of core beliefs using an approach that critically engages with biblical text
Gain knowledge and understanding of a range of religions and worldviews appreciating diversity, continuity and change within the religions and worldviews being studied
Engage with challenging questions of meaning and purpose raised by human existence and experience
Recognise the concept of religion and its continuing influence on Britain’s cultural heritage and in the lives of individuals and societies in different times, cultures and places
Explore their own religious, spiritual and philosophical ways of living, believing and thinking
RE in Nursery
During their time spent in the Nursery, children will have opportunities to find out and learn about the world they live in. These experiences may include:
Learning about themselves within the context of their Church school
Learning about the beliefs and cultures of others
Encountering the celebration of different festivals, including the celebrations connected with being part of a Church school
Hearing stories from the Bible, and, where appropriate, from other cultural and religious traditions.
RE in Reception and Key Stage One
In Surrey our aims for RE are..
To enable pupils to:
• Demonstrate an appreciation of the nature of worldviews and the important contribution of religion and belief, spiritual insights and values to the individual’s search for meaning in life
• Recognise that someone’s worldview, including their own, can be influenced by many factors and is an intrinsic part of how they view the world
• Develop knowledge and understanding of Christianity, and of the other principal religions and beliefs represented in Great Britain, through their history, contemporary diverse expressions and encountering peoples’ lived experience
• Develop interest in and enthusiasm for the study of worldviews and enhance their own spiritual, moral, social and cultural development
• Develop the ability to make reasoned, informed and creative responses to religious and moral issues
• Recognise the influence of beliefs, values and traditions on the individual, on culture and on communities throughout the world
Expanding Young Horizons
Expanding Young Horizons

Subjects> Writing
Curriculum focus
Writing
Intent
The aim of our writing curriculum is to provide every child with the opportunity to become an accurate and fluent writer.
Being able to communicate in the modern world, through handwritten or typed text is as vital now as it has ever been. In school children at Chilworth Infants are encouraged to write in a variety of different genres ranging from creative story writing to non-chronological reports. We ensure that children write for a variety of audiences and for a wide range of purposes. This approach has shown to increase their confidence in writing.
Implementation
We plan in 3 stages: long-term, medium-term and short-term. Our long-term planning follows the National Curriculum. Our medium-term planning is done on a half termly basis. This planning reflects the outcomes of regular assessment of the areas that have been taught and is adapted to the needs of the current cohort. Short term planning is completed for each week.
Our writing curriculum runs closely alongside our reading curriculum. Good phonological knowledge is a fundamental skill in spelling which is an integral part of writing. From the very beginning at Chilworth C of E Infant School, pupils are taught systematic synthetic phonics through our chosen scheme, Little Wandle. This provides the building blocks of letters through our daily phonics sessions. These sessions include segmenting and blending skills. Additionally, children are taught a series of high frequency tricky words as whole sight vocabulary.
To be able to write well is closely linked to spoken language and reading competence. Our writing curriculum is carefully planned to take into consideration a child’s reading ability and level of language acquisition. We work with a range of well selected and high-quality literacy texts to model to the children exciting and ambitious vocabulary and written text. This includes, fiction, non-fiction, poetry, rhymes, plays and traditional tales.
Children’s writing is assessed on a half termly basis and enables the school to identity and offer additional support for those children in need of it. We work closely with ‘Specialist Teachers for Inclusive Practice’ who provide advice and support for those children for whom we are concerned.
Impact
Our children make good progress as they journey from Nursery to Year 2. Our end of Key Stage 1 results demonstrate we have a successful system of delivering writing as these results are consistently above national averages.

Special Educational Needs (SENCo)
At Chilworth Infant school we want all of our children to be supported and challenged to develop a love of learning.
Sometimes our pupils may need additional support in school. Mrs. Whiteley our SEND coordinator works alongside parents, outside professionals, and our team to ensure that in these cases children and their parents have the support and guidance they need.
Tara Whiteley - Special Educational Needs coordinator (SENCo)
Send coffee meetings
Once a term we hold a SEND parent coffee morning.
Below are some of the topics we have discussed at previous coffee mornings:
helpful home routines
family relationships
accessing support in the local area for your family / child
Supporting your children with their social and emotional needs
We look forward to seeing you there at the next one.
Send Clinics
A week or two before our parent - teacher interviews, parents of students with SEND are invited to attend an extra meeting to discuss their progress in relation to their SEND targets.
ELSA - Emotional Literacy Support Assistant
An ELSA is a specialist Teaching Assistant who has been trained to work with children who are showing a wide range of emotional or social difficulties, for example;
problems with anger or regulating their emotions
ELSAs are chosen for their ability to build good relationships with children.
WHAT ISSUES MAY BE COVERED DURING SESSIONS?
Any issue which may interfere with a child’s learning, is worth supporting.
An emotionally happy child is one that will enjoy their lessons, feel confident and thrive at school.
Some specific issues that may be covered are:
WHAT DOES AN ELSA DO AND HOW DO THEY SUPPORT CHILDREN?
An ELSA works closely with teachers to set clear objectives for children.
The ELSA will then work on these objectives with the child individually or in a small group.
Activities, which target the needs of the child, are planned carefully by the ELSA.
ELSA sessions are planned in advance and tailor made to suit the needs of the children.
Sessions are designed to be fun and interactive and to engage and motivate the child. A range of activities may be used which could include role play, games, puppets, outdoor learning, Art and Crafts as well as talking and listening.

Tips for helping your child at drop off
NSPCC Positive Parenting guide
Supporting attention, activity & behaviour

Our Governors
Every school has a Governing Body, which sets the strategic framework for the School and works in partnership with the Headteacher.
This includes setting the overall objectives and monitoring progress. The Governing Body works with the Head, who is responsible for the day-to-day running of the school including the management of the staff. Governors need to fulfil their statutory duties and ensure that the school complies with the statutory framework.
Who we are:
We are a group of volunteers who represent the school and wider community - Parents, Staff, Church, Diocese, and Local Authority. Foundation Governors of a church school also have to ensure that the school's distinctively Christian character is maintained.
All Governors though, along with the Headteacher and Staff, aim to ensure that the school provides education of the highest quality within the context of Christian belief and practice. It encourages an understanding of the meaning and significance of faith and promotes Christian values through the experience it offers all its pupils. Governors usually sit for a term of 4 years (often with the opportunity to put their names forward for re-appointment when this period ends), and the Chairman and Vice Chairman are elected annually by the Governing Body.
Should you at any stage require information about governor related matters please e-mail Sarah Stevens or Andrew Pearson at info@chilworth.surrey.sch.uk or look at the Governors' Board in the school Entrance Lobby.
Governors work with the Headteacher to:
Promote an ambitious vision for the school and high expectations of all pupils and teachers
Improve the school and develop its capacity for sustained improvement by helping to develop high quality teaching, leadership capacity and high professional standards among all staff
Ensure that all teaching staff benefit from appropriate professional development and that performance is rigorously managed
Accurately evaluate the school’s strengths and weaknesses and use their findings to promote improvement
Provide a broad and balanced curriculum that meets the needs of all pupils, enables all pupils to achieve their full educational potential and make progress in their learning, and promotes their good behaviour and safety and their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development
Promote pupils’ learning and progress in literacy and numeracy
Engage with parents in supporting pupils’ achievement, behaviour and safety and their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development
Take steps to promote the safety of all pupils and ensure that they are safe in school
Our Committees
Our Governing Body meets in separate committees as well as collectively throughout the year.
Their mandate is to ensure that our school is delivering the best possible education to every child and they assure themselves that this is happening by regularly visiting classes and teachers in school as well as asking questions.
There are 4 main committees that meet termly.
Curriculum and Standards Committee
The purpose of this committee is to ensure that the education at our school is of a consistently high standard. This group ensures that the school are accomplishing what they have committed to in areas of development identified in the school development plan. They assure themselves that this is the case by briefings from the teachers and by being in school and seeing for themselves.
The purpose of this committee is to ensure that there is consistently good stewardship of all the school’s resources, both human and financial. By close monitoring of the budget as well as ensuring all areas of HR are fairly managed, they can assure themselves that we as a school are good stewards.
Buildings, Health and Safety Committee
The purpose of this committee is to ensure that the infrastructure of our school is always in the best standard of repair. By regularly undertaking site checks they can assure themselves that the school site is being maintained and improved.
Safeguarding Committee
The purpose of this committee is to ensure that safeguarding in school is robust. They ensure that all those who work with the school have been DBS checked and completed regular training. They ensure that there is a culture of safeguarding that permeates the school and all who work in it. They assure themselves that this is the case by regular check ins with staff and pupils.
